high.title: Four Largest Banks in the System Raise Savings Interest Rates, Some Terms Increase by 1.2%/Year
high.summary: Vietnam Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (Agribank) has raised deposit interest rates across multiple terms, with the highest rate now reaching 6.5%/year for 24-month deposits, up from 5.3%/year previously. Short-term rates (1-2 months) increased 0.2 percentage points to 2.6%/year, while 3-5 month terms rose to 2.9%/year. Mid-term deposits (6-11 months) were raised 0.2 points to 4.0%/year. The most significant increase was in longer terms: 12-18 month deposits jumped 0.7 points to 5.9%/year, and 24-month terms surged 1.2 points to 6.5%/year. This follows similar moves by other major state-owned banks including Vietinbank, BIDV, and VietcomBank, signaling coordinated monetary tightening. For FX and bond traders, this represents clear hawkish pressure from funding cost increases, likely putting upward pressure on VND money market rates and potentially supporting VND against USD while creating headwinds for Vietnamese government bond prices as deposit rates become more competitive with sovereign yields.

high.title: Is the Worst Period for the Stock Market Over?
high.summary: The VN-Index has gained 67 points over two sessions, completely recovering losses from Monday's gap-down opening. Markets showed stronger upward momentum on March 25 with broad-based gains and improved liquidity, suggesting investor sentiment has stabilized significantly after the recent sharp decline. A major concern for investors has been Middle East tensions disrupting energy supply chains, with oil prices surging and creating multiple negative impacts including higher costs eroding corporate profits, inflation weakening economic purchasing power, and USD strength pressuring exchange rates and monetary policy. The positive development is that Middle East tensions show signs of cooling, with warring parties beginning to discuss negotiations rather than military escalation. Oil prices have reversed sharply lower. For VND traders and government bond investors, this market recovery suggests reduced risk-off pressure on Vietnamese assets, potentially supporting VND stability and reducing safe-haven demand that had been pressuring local bond yields higher.

high.title: Bank Q1/2026 Profit Forecast: VietinBank, BIDV and HDBank Leading Growth
high.summary: Vietcombank Securities forecasts Q1/2026 banking sector results will show slower growth due to funding cost pressure on net interest margins (NIM), while credit room limitations particularly impact real estate lending. Private banks are expected to see reduced growth rates, while state-owned banks appear more promising due to low funding cost advantages and a low 2025 profit base. BIDV is forecast to achieve Q1 operating income of VND20.833 trillion (+16%) and pre-tax profit of VND9.366 trillion (+26%), with full-year 2026 pre-tax profit potentially reaching VND43.435 trillion (+15%). VietinBank is projected for Q1 pre-tax profit of VND13.5 trillion (+23%), while the banking sector overall faces NIM compression from 2.8% to 2.5-2.6% range. This banking sector analysis is crucial for VND traders as it indicates potential pressure on bank funding costs could support higher interbank rates, strengthening VND, while government bond yields may face upward pressure as banks compete more aggressively for deposits.

medium.title: Trump Extends Pause on Attacks on Iran's Energy Facilities for Additional 10 Days at 'Iran's Request'
medium.summary: President Trump announced a 10-day extension of the pause on attacks against Iran's energy facilities until April 6, following requests from Iran's government. This avoids war escalation while the Strait of Hormuz remains largely closed to oil transport. Oil prices were rising when the announcement was made. This development reduces geopolitical risk premium, potentially supporting risk appetite for emerging market assets including Vietnamese dong and equities.

medium.title: SJC Gold and Plain Gold Ring Prices on Morning of March 26
medium.summary: Gold prices at major Vietnamese dealers like DOJI, PNJ, and Bao Tin Manh Hai are quoted at VND170.5-173.5 million per tael for both SJC gold and plain gold rings. Bao Tin Minh Chau maintains higher prices at VND172.5-175.0 million per tael after temporarily closing some Hanoi stores for cooperation with authorities. International gold prices are near $4,400/ounce, equivalent to about VND141 million per tael excluding taxes and fees. The significant premium of domestic gold over international prices indicates continued capital flow restrictions and potential VND weakness concerns.

medium.title: China Just Received Great News from Vietnam
medium.summary: Vietnam remains one of China's largest fruit import markets, with grape imports alone reaching $220 million USD in 2025 despite a 17% decline. Vietnam topped grape import values ahead of Indonesia ($150M), Thailand ($140M), Philippines ($90M) and Russia ($80M). This trade relationship demonstrates continued strong bilateral commercial ties and Vietnam's position as a key consumption market, which supports broader trade balance dynamics affecting VND/USD over the medium term.

medium.title: Vietnam Continuously Receives Good News from the US and Japan
medium.summary: Vietnam's scallop export value reached nearly $66 million in 2025, up 49% from $44 million in 2024, with acceleration in early 2026 showing $18.1 million in two months (+166% YoY). Japan emerged as the fastest-growing market at $14 million (+173%), while the US maintained $13.8 million (+10%). This export growth supports Vietnam's trade balance and foreign currency earnings, providing fundamental support for VND stability.
